newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy "Euro Tax" won't hit business--Fin Min Visco.
newsitem.headline: Italy "Euro Tax" won't hit business--Fin Min Visco.

text.p: The so-called "Euro Tax", which the government hopes will raise 13 trillion lire next year, will not hurt business, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco was quoted as saying on Thursday.

The Treasury has said the Euro Tax will be a one-off measure designed at helping Italy meet tough deficit demands imposed by the Maastricht Treaty on countries wishing to be founder members of the planned single European currency.
However it has not yet outlined how the tax will work.
"The only thing I can say is that it will not weigh on productive activity," Visco told La Stampa newspaper.

Besides the Euro Tax, the Treasury has yet to explain how it will raise a further 4.2 trillion lire in fresh revenues next year. The media has speculated that much of the money will come from higher value added tax.
But Visco said the planned measures would not have "a significant impact" on prices. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
